top_authentic_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_authentic_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 84.6% authentic and 15.4% AI, a extremely high-confidence finding toward real camera capture.
top_authentic_signals.what_found: Across all six lenses, the model returned only 15.4% AI probability, consistent with real camera optics. The SRM residuals match expected sensor noise, the FFT spectrum shows natural frequency falloff (no periodic grid artifacts), and the SPAI reconstruction probe behaved the way natural scenes respond, not the way AI-synthesized regions do.
top_authentic_signals.why_it_matters: A 84.6% authenticity score means the image's deepest mathematical structure is consistent with physical lens optics and silicon sensor physics. AI generators produce fundamentally different frequency-domain statistics than cameras, and those differences persist even when the image looks visually convincing.
top_authentic_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.

top_ai_signals.name: Metadata & Provenance
top_ai_signals.summary: The file's embedded provenance marks it as AI-generated.
top_ai_signals.what_found: The embedded metadata names a generative tool: veo.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Provenance markers like C2PA are an industry-standard, hard-to-fake trace written by the generator itself. Finding one is among the strongest provenance signals available.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Provenance can be stripped or, rarely, forged. Absence of a marker is not proof of authenticity.

top_ai_signals.name: Lighting Physics & Contrast Geometry
top_ai_signals.summary: The lighting looks physically impossible for a real camera: dynamic range of 255/255 with only 0.005% blown highlights and 0.084% crushed shadows.
top_ai_signals.what_found: This image spans 255/255 of tonal range but loses virtually no detail at either extreme - 0.005% clipped highlights and 0.084% crushed shadows. Real camera sensors physically cannot do this: they must sacrifice highlight or shadow detail in high-contrast scenes. The regional contrast variance of 459.7 is also suspiciously low, meaning light is distributed unnaturally evenly across the entire scene.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This 'perfect HDR' profile is a known fingerprint of AI generation. Diffusion models compute light mathematically and don't face the physical saturation limits that real sensors do. A camera would always clip in one or both directions here.
top_ai_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Thermal Noise & Sensor Consistency
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The noise profile is ambiguous - variance 957.6, 12.2% smooth blocks - midrange values that could belong to either a compressed real photo or a noise-augmented AI image.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: The image has variance 957.6 and 12.2% flat blocks - neither extreme enough to trigger a clear verdict. This ambiguity typically means the image has been compressed, resized, or otherwise processed in a way that erased the original noise fingerprint.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: When noise falls in the middle range, it can belong to either side - meaning this signal cannot meaningfully contribute to the verdict. The other detectors carry more weight here.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, upscaling, or added grain filters can all change the noise profile independently of whether the image was generated or photographed.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Error Level Analysis (ELA)
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The ELA map shows moderate, fairly uniform compression residuals (mean: 0.87, quadrant spread: 0.11). No editing seams or compositing artifacts were detected.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: Re-saving at quality 90 produced a mean residual of 0.87 with a quadrant spread of only 0.11. The compression stress is consistent across all four quadrants, and only 0.00% of pixels show elevated residuals. This uniform profile suggests the image has a consistent compression history - no obvious signs of region-level editing or compositing.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: A uniform ELA profile removes one red flag - there are no obvious editing seams. However, ELA does not tell us whether the image is AI-generated, only that it has not been obviously composited. The other detectors handle the AI vs. real question.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: ELA detects editing and compression inconsistency, not AI generation. Social media uploads, repeated saves, and WhatsApp forwarding all degrade this test. It's treated as a weak supporting check.
